pr_title: [Transform] implement retention policy to delete data from a transform
pr_body:
add a retention policy to transform to delete data that is considered outdated as part of a transform checkpoint.

fixes #67916

issue_context.title: [Transform] add the ability to delete documents from the destination index
issue_context.body:
Transform provides a persistent view on data by pivoting them or providing the latest state. With "continuous mode" this view gets updated and kept up-to-date.

However, transform keeps adding _new_ data. However you might want to age out old data or remove data from the persistent view on other criteria. Especially for `latest` we see a lack of functionality. With `latest` you might want to delete entities that haven't been seen for a longer period. E.g. if you transform host information you might want to remove decommissioned hosts.

## Overall integration

Retention will be part of the overall transform configuration:

```
{
    "source": { ... },
    "dest": { ... },

    "pivot": { ... },   
OR  
    "latest": { ... },
    "retention_policy": {
        "name": {...}
    }
```

Therefore, `retention_policy` will be available for both `pivot` _and_ `latest`.

The choice for nesting at an extra level gives us an extension point for later. The first `retention_policy` to be implemented is `time`:

## Time based retention

```
    "retention_policy": {
        "time": {
            "field": "@timestamp",
            "max_age": "30d"
        }
    }
```

This policy requires you to configure a timestamp field (likely the same field as used for `sync`) and a `max_age`. Data that is older than `max_age` is considered outdated and will be removed as part of checkpointing:

## Retention integration into checkpoints

Retention will be implemented as last step of checkpointing, that means it runs at the final phase of checkpointing. When a checkpoint is completed, data that should be deleted as defined by the policy. Retention is calculated based on the checkpoint time.

## Retention policy updating

Updating the retention policy is supported by `_update`. If `_update` is called on a _running_ transform, update gets effective when a new checkpoint gets started. The currently running checkpoint will use the _current_ policy.

FYI: @elastic/ml-ui it would be good to support retention policy in the update fly-out

## Retention policy stats

For measuring the retention policy we add 2 counters to `_stats`:

`documents_deleted`

Total number of documents deleted in the transform destination index by this transform.

`delete_time_in_ms`

Cumulative sum of time spend deleting documents in the transform destination index by this transform.

review_comments: this change is unnecessary. I am not sure ES server actions like this follow the same formatting yet.
no, it isn't. The change here is the addition of `public`, which is necessary for testing and I think it is ok to make it `public`. Formatting is the result of line length overflow.
Could you add the appropriate line for the added category below?

As long as it doesn't hit performance, I prefer using proper time-relates types (`java.time`) instead of performing calculations directly (like division by 1000000).
Could these types be used here?

I implemented it the same way as the others, see:
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/master/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/indexing/IndexerJobStats.java#L172

I don't want to do it differently than the other places. I agree about using time instead of low-level types, I might change it in _all_ places as a follow up.
Do we want to call `getStats().markEndDelete();` even on failures? I am not sure how the stats react here.

I followed the design pattern of `AsyncTwoPhaseIndexer` - also w.r.t. naming etc. We have a similar situation for search and indexing, on a failure the global counters are _not_ incremented. Stats are fine, too: when `markStart{Indexing/Search/Delete}` is called a member variable gets set, if you call it twice, this member gets reset without incrementing the global counter.

it might also be good to log if there were bulk failures. (debug level for the full messages). 

I think it is possible (even with retries turned off) where the bulk scroll response has errors in it but still returns an "OK".
this is the renamed `TransformIndexerTests`, no changes done
Wouldn't this cause problems when other types of policies are added in subsequent versions?

You could add the accessors to `RetentionPolicyConfig` so that you don't have to do this casting.

Or `RetentionPolicyConfig` know everything about itself it could have a `toDeleteByQueryRequest` method

Yeah it would? I think thats the idea. If you add a new policy, you sure better make sure to write a request converter. 

Throwing here is a good pattern. It enforces case handling.

> Or RetentionPolicyConfig know everything about itself it could have a toDeleteByQueryRequest method

Intentionally I avoided that. We had (probably still have) a lot of logic in the config classes in the past and I had a hard time to separate config and logic.

I agree it looks a little dumb at the moment, its just 1 config with 1 implementation.
I moved the former `TransformIndexerTests` to `TransformIndexerFailureHandlingTests`, so this is a new file.
Is there any integration test added for the new functionality? I couldn't find it in this PR and I think it would be beneficial.

I had a hard time to craft one, I don't want to slow down the test execution further. It would be nice to manipulate the clock, but I think that's hard to do from the outside. E.g. I defined that `max_age` _must_ be at least `60s`. So an integration test _must_ run at least `60s`.

What I did:

- unit test: test a policy is translated to a delete by query
- module test: test that the indexer is calling the delete extension points if a policy is there and not if a policy is `null` -> ensures the right hooks are called at the end of the checkpoint. see the new `TransformIndexerTests`

out of scope:

- testing correctness of delete by query
